intent: To illustrate the relationship between educational attainment and Black migration rates from the South, highlighting the significance of 'some college' education in this trend since the 1960s.

requirements.question: Must the video explicitly identify Some college as the top category?
Must the full rank order be conveyed, or is only the top category's position required?
Should the video explicitly contrast Some college with College graduate as the top two categories?

units.claim: Some college is the highest educational-attainment category by value/relative_value.

basis.note: maximum value among the four categories
maximum relative_value among the four categories

accept: Some college has the largest value, 27.
Some college is the top category, with relative_value 0.6525.
The tallest/largest bar is Some college.
units.evidence: The Some college mark must be visually identifiable as the largest/tallest/longest among the four categories.

units.claim: The four categories order from highest to lowest as Some college, College graduate, High school graduate, Less than high school.
accept: The categories rank as Some college > College graduate > High school graduate > Less than high school.
College graduate is second, High school graduate third, and Less than high school fourth.
The bars are ordered from Some college down to Less than high school.
units.evidence: The relative heights/lengths of all four categories must make the full rank order visible.

units.claim: Some college's value (27) is greater than College graduate's value (20), so the 'some college' category is the top category above 'college graduate'.
accept: Some college is higher than College graduate.
Some college exceeds College graduate by 7.
Some college is about 1.35 times College graduate.
units.evidence: The Some college bar must be visibly taller/longer than the College graduate bar.

optional_valid: Showing exact relative_value labels 0.6525, 0.4834, 0.2175, 0.0725 for the four categories.
